Container.Name: OpenThread-Border-Router
Container.Overview:
The official OpenThread Border Router (OTBR) image from the OpenThread project (Google). It turns a USB Thread radio flashed with OpenThread RCP firmware into a Thread border router for Matter-over-Thread and Thread devices, with a REST API for Home Assistant's OpenThread Border Router integration and a small web UI. It is the plain upstream image; the separate OpenThreadBorderRouter-HA template in this repository uses the Home Assistant add-on build instead. Run only one of them per radio.
**1. Radio firmware**
The USB stick must run OpenThread **RCP** firmware (not Zigbee, not multiprotocol). Home Assistant Connect ZBT-1/SkyConnect and ZBT-2: flash the OpenThread firmware with https://toolbox.openhomefoundation.org/ (460800 baud with hardware flow control, Home Assistant's default). Other radios such as the nRF52840 dongle: see https://openthread.io/platforms and use the baud rate of your firmware. The baud rate and flow control in OT_RCP_DEVICE must match the firmware.
**2. Unraid network settings**
- Settings > Network Settings: Network protocol **IPv4 + IPv6**, and IPv6 address assignment **Automatic**. - The container must use **host** networking; Thread devices are reached over IPv6 routes on your LAN interface (usually `br0`, or `eth0`/`bond0` without bridging).
**3. Host kernel settings (required)**
OTBR needs IPv6 forwarding on the host, and the LAN interface must keep accepting router advertisements while forwarding (accept_ra=2), otherwise Unraid loses its own IPv6 address and Thread devices become unreachable. Docker cannot set these with --sysctl in host network mode (that is why they are not in Extra Parameters). Run on the host, replacing br0 with your interface:
`sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1` `sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding=1` `sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.br0.accept_ra=2` `sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.br0.accept_ra_rt_info_max_plen=64`
Unraid resets these at reboot and when DHCP renews the interface, so put them in a User Scripts script that runs **At Startup of Array** and also on a custom schedule such as `*/5 * * * *`.
**4. Container settings**
- Radio: pick your stick under /dev/serial/by-id/ (stable across reboots) and keep `:/dev/ttyUSB0` at the end so it appears as /dev/ttyUSB0 inside the container. - `/dev/net/tun` and the NET_ADMIN capability (Extra Parameters) are needed to create the wpan0 interface and the firewall/NAT64 rules. Privileged mode is not needed. - Thread credentials are stored in the Data folder; back it up. Losing it means re-pairing every device.
**5. Home Assistant**
Add the **OpenThread Border Router** integration with URL `http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:8081`, then the **Thread** integration. Under Settings > Devices > Thread, form a network or make this the preferred network and send the credentials to your phone for Matter commissioning. Phones and Home Assistant must be able to route IPv6 to your LAN.
**Image tag:** `stable` is the monthly release (vYYYY.MM.0). `latest` is rebuilt on every commit and can break, so use it only to test a fix. Pin a version (e.g. `openthread/border-router:v2026.11.0`) if you want to control upgrades.
**Security:** the REST API (port 8081) and web UI have no authentication and can change or read the Thread network key. Keep them on your LAN; set OT_REST_LISTEN_ADDR to 127.0.0.1 if Home Assistant also runs in host network mode on this server.
Docs: https://openthread.io/guides/border-router/docker · Home Assistant: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/otbr/

Container.Requires: A Thread USB radio flashed with OpenThread RCP firmware Unraid IPv6 enabled and the host sysctls from the Overview applied

Config.Name: Radio (USB device)
Config.Description: Host path of your RCP radio, followed by :/dev/ttyUSB0. Find it with ls -l /dev/serial/by-id/ (ZBT-1/SkyConnect show as usb-Nabu_Casa_SkyConnect...).

Config.Name: TUN Device
Config.Description: Required to create the Thread network interface (wpan0).

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Thread network credentials and settings (keep a backup).

Config.Name: RCP Device URL
Config.Description: Radio URL. Home Assistant ZBT-1/SkyConnect/ZBT-2: 460800 with uart-flow-control. For other radios use the baud rate of your firmware and remove &uart-flow-control if it has no flow control.

Config.Name: Infrastructure Interface
Config.Description: Host LAN interface Thread is routed to (br0, eth0, bond0 or a VLAN like br0.3). Use the interface that has your LAN IPv6 address.

Config.Name: Thread Interface
Config.Description: Name of the Thread network interface created on the host. Change only if wpan0 already exists.

Config.Name: REST API Address
Config.Description: Address for the REST API used by Home Assistant. 0.0.0.0 = reachable on the LAN; 127.0.0.1 = this server only.

Config.Name: REST API Port
Config.Description: REST API port (Home Assistant integration URL http://[IP]:8081).

Config.Name: Web UI Address
Config.Description: Address for the OTBR web UI. Set 127.0.0.1 to disable LAN access.

Config.Name: Web UI Port
Config.Description: OTBR web UI port. Unraid uses 80, and 8080 is often taken, so 28080 is the default here.

Config.Name: Log Level
Config.Description: otbr-agent log level 0-7 (4 = warning, 6 = info, 7 = debug, very noisy).

Config.Name: Vendor Name
Config.Description: Vendor name advertised over mDNS and shown in Home Assistant.

Config.Name: Model Name
Config.Description: Model name advertised over mDNS and shown in Home Assistant.
